checks_run.procedure: Judge BE-Z6's re-raise rule (hidden conflict, lost system update, stale human overwrite). Then walk the escalation and the reports as a user who may (TO) and a user who may not (TL) see the benefit, in en and ar.
checks_run.command: Read apps/api/src/modules/operations/exceptions.ts (rebaseOverSystemOccurrences, acknowledgeException, resolveException, raiseOperationalException), the 0101 history trigger, ADR-0053 §2 and the BE-Z6 handback; exception-recurrence-race.test.ts runs in DOM-R5-07; e2e/a22-p6-operability.spec.ts runs in DOM-R5-08; dom-r5-screens.spec.ts part B screenshots
checks_run.environment: Repository and clone at d7b21bad3; production-initialized stack with the production worker; Chromium.
checks_run.expected: No real conflict is hidden, no system update is lost, and no stale human write overwrites a newer human one. Each user's outcome is still useful.
checks_run.actual: BE-Z6 meets the operating logic. The rebase is accepted only when every version after the loaded one has a history row whose kind is 'recurred' with a null actor, with no gap. The 0101 trigger classifies an update as 'recurred' only when the status did not change. So any human acknowledge or resolve, an automatic 'recovered' resolution, or an 'updated' event gives 409. A human-vs-human conflict therefore stays 409 in either order. The UPDATE applies to the locked row and sets only the status fields, so the recurrence's count, last occurrence and last error are kept: no system update is lost. The audit event records based_on_version. One consequence is acceptable but undocumented: a human can resolve an exception that recurred after their page loaded. That occurrence stays counted on the resolved row, and the next failure opens a new exception (ADR-0053 'After resolution, a new failure opens a new row'), so the signal returns at the next occurrence; failure-queue rows also stay visible. A raiser acting with a human actor would be conservatively rejected (409), which loses nothing. ADR-0053 §2 was not amended, as the handback requested: raised as F-DG6-341 (Low, documentation). Usefulness: for TL (not admitted), in en and ar, the executive-decision list and detail show 'DEC-01 · CA-01' with origin 'From a blocker escalation', and the case link gives the not-found state. That is enough to know an escalation exists and to ask the TO. For the TO (admitted), the same ask is followed to the case, which shows the benefit title. The ask's owner is unassigned on this stack ('Owner unassigned', with 'Decision owner' listed as missing), the DG4 behaviour where no owner rule applies. A non-admitted SP who owns such an ask sees only the case code. The TO can grant access, and the alternative (the title in every reader's ask) is the leak F-DG6-280 closed. I accept it. The traceability, missing-links and G6 outcomes were judged in DOM-R5-04. The report outcome is F-DG6-340.
